# North Shelf status: 27 kits counted, none released

## 1. Short answers to your five questions

How many kits can we send, and when will they arrive? Harbor Depot holds 27 water-treatment kits, but none is released, so we can't send any yet. There is no arrival date. The release desk does not give release dates in advance.

When will the other 13 come? The sources don't say. Our count of 27 doesn't fill your request for 40, and nothing on file says when or whether more kits will come.

Can you send your own vehicle during the documentation window? No. The window is for paperwork questions only. Until a release is recorded, the clinic must not send a vehicle to collect kits.

Whom do you call about release timing? Nobody can give you a date yet. When a release is recorded, the release desk tells the Field Clinic S-3 supply clerk directly. The paperwork line is for paperwork questions only.

What can you tell patients? Don't tell them that treatment water is coming. The sources give no other wording for patients.

## 2. What you asked for and what we hold

The North Shelf request is on file. The Field Clinic S-3 supply clerk asked Harbor Depot for 40 water-treatment kits, and the request notes that the clinic's water point uses about 20 kits a week. A request on file does not schedule a pickup or a delivery, and no delivery date is set.

Harbor Depot holds 27 water-treatment kits, counted and staged in pen 4. Every kit is sealed, and no carton is damaged. Counted and staged is custody, not a release: the kits are accounted for, but they can't leave pen 4 until a release is recorded.

## 3. What a release needs

A release takes three steps, each done by a different office. The release desk releases a lot, the transport desk assigns a vehicle, and the permit office approves a permit. The release desk records a release only when all three are done.

Ivo Marsh at the Harbor Depot release desk owns any release. The inventory clerk does not own it, and neither does your supply clerk. The release desk does not give release dates in advance. When it records a release, it tells the Field Clinic S-3 supply clerk directly, so you'll hear from the release desk, not from this brief.

## 4. Where things stand now

None of the three steps has happened. No lot is released. No vehicle is assigned. A permit is approved. No receipt is confirmed. Whether the movement is supportable is unknown.

Truck HS-3 is parked in bay 2, and HS-3 is not assigned to any request. The yard board shows where vehicles are parked. It doesn't assign a vehicle to a request, so HS-3 being in the yard says nothing about North Shelf.

## 5. What the clinic must not do yet

Until a release is recorded, the clinic must not schedule kit use. The clinic must not tell patients that treatment water is coming. The clinic must not send a vehicle to collect kits. The clinic must not treat the documentation window as a time the kits will arrive.

These limits hold even though the kits are counted and sealed. A count shows where the kits are. It doesn't release them.

## 6. Paperwork questions and contact

For paperwork questions, call 555-0194 during the documentation window: Thursday and Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Calls outside the window are not answered. A paperwork question is something like a correction to the request record or a question about the count sheet. The window is not a pickup appointment, a dispatch, or a delivery promise. This brief is for the Field Clinic S-3 supply team only.
